BC.name: Budget check on purchase requests
BC.summary: Before a purchase request goes through, its month must have enough budget left. These rules say which month counts and what has already been used.

BU.name: Budgets and the Master Budget
BU.summary: The Master Budget caps each department for the year. No budget may go over it.

BR.name: Changing budgets
BR.summary: Budgets come from an upload, and change through a reallocation or a mid year file. These rules keep every change within the limits and on record.

RP.name: Budget reports
RP.summary: The reports show the same figures the checks use, so a user can see in advance what will pass.

PR.name: Purchase requests
PR.summary: An employee asks for a purchase. These rules fill in the cost center and account, and make sure a budget exists.

SQ.name: Quotations
SQ.summary: Vendors quote against a request. A quotation may never be higher than what was approved.

PO.name: Purchase orders and receipts
PO.summary: Procurement orders from the vendor. Every order goes back to a request.

PI.name: Purchase invoices
PI.summary: Finance books the vendor's invoice against its order.

PE.name: Payments
PE.summary: Accounts payable pays vendors and employees, always against something that is due.

EC.name: Expense claims
EC.summary: An employee claims money spent. The claim uses the budget of the employee's department.

AT.name: Attendance and shifts
AT.summary: Check-ins, shifts, Saturdays and the attendance sheet sent to payroll.

LV.name: Leave, probation and contracts
LV.summary: Leave earned at the end of probation, and the monthly reminders to managers and HR.

PY.name: Salary slips and payslip import
PY.summary: How salary slips are emailed, and how the payroll vendor's files are imported.

WF.name: Approval workflows
WF.summary: Who approves each document, and in what order.

AC.name: Who sees what
AC.summary: Which records each role finds in its lists.

ED.name: EOMS documents
ED.summary: Documents everyone reads in the Desk, page by page, without downloading them. Only system managers add or change them.

TR.name: Training videos and user manuals
TR.summary: Each training topic has a short video, a user manual or both, that every employee opens on the site. Only system managers add or change them.

VN.name: Vendors
VN.summary: How vendors are registered and numbered.

EM.name: Emails and letter heads
EM.summary: Emails and letter heads follow the company of the document.

DB.name: Dashboards
DB.summary: What each dashboard shows, and for which companies.

ST.name: Set up on the site
ST.summary: Rules made directly on the site, not in the app. They were read on the date shown in the catalogue. The tables below show the site as it is now.

XX.name: Keeping rules true
XX.summary: The rules, this page and the tests always agree. A check fails when they drift apart.

BC-01.title: A request uses the month it is raised in
BC-01.plain: A purchase request uses the budget of the month of its transaction date, not the month the goods are needed. A request raised in March for April uses the March budget.

BC-02.title: With that setting off, the required date counts
BC-02.plain: When the setting is switched off, the standard check uses the month the goods are required by.

BC-03.title: A request stays within its own month's budget
BC-03.plain: A request may use exactly what its month has left and not a rupee more. Money left over from earlier months cannot be used. A month with no budget blocks every request.

BC-04.title: With that setting off, earlier months roll on
BC-04.plain: When the setting is switched off, unused budget of earlier months can be used, as in standard ERPNext.

BC-05.title: How a month's budget is worked out
BC-05.plain: A month gets its share of the year from the budget's monthly split. A budget with no split gives each month one twelfth.

BC-06.title: An account with no budget is not checked by month
BC-06.plain: The monthly check looks only at accounts that have a budget for requests. Another rule already refuses a request with no budget at all (see PR-06).

BC-07.title: Rows on one account are added up first
BC-07.plain: A request cannot pass by splitting an amount over several rows. Rows on the same account and cost center are checked together.

BC-08.title: Only purchase requests use budget
BC-08.plain: A request for a transfer or an issue of material does not use budget.

BC-09.title: A request is counted once
BC-09.plain: An approved request uses its full amount at once. Its order, invoice and payment do not use the budget again.

BC-10.title: A stopped request gives back what was not ordered
BC-10.plain: Stopping a request frees the part that was not ordered. A request stopped when half is ordered keeps half.

BC-11.title: Cancelled and rejected requests use nothing
BC-11.plain: Cancelling or rejecting a request frees its budget. Cancelling only the order keeps the request, which still uses the budget.

BC-12.title: Expense claims use budget when approved
BC-12.plain: An approved claim uses the amount that was sanctioned, in the month of its date. Draft and rejected claims use nothing.

BC-13.title: Journal entries use budget
BC-13.plain: A journal entry booked to a budgeted account uses its budget in its month. A correcting entry moves the use from one account to the other, so nothing is counted twice.

BC-14.title: No backdated requests
BC-14.plain: A request cannot be dated before today. A draft raised on an earlier day can still be approved later.

BC-15.title: Older requests keep the month they were checked in
BC-15.plain: When an effective date is set, requests raised before it are counted in the month they were required by.

BC-16.title: The year runs from April to March
BC-16.plain: Monthly figures follow the fiscal year, April to March.

BC-17.title: The checks work on older and newer ERPNext
BC-17.plain: The budget checks give the same answer before and after the ERPNext upgrade.

BC-18.title: Open requests are added up row by row
BC-18.plain: On older ERPNext, each open request row is counted at its own rate.

BC-19.title: Standard budget control still applies
BC-19.plain: ERPNext's own budget control stays in force for orders, invoices and journal entries. With all settings off, requests follow it too.

BU-01.title: Each department is listed once
BU-01.plain: A Master Budget lists each department only once.

BU-02.title: Departments stay within the total
BU-02.plain: The department budgets added together cannot be more than the total of the Master Budget.

BU-03.title: No budget goes over the Master Budget
BU-03.plain: All budgets of a cost center together stay within its row in the Master Budget, however the budget was made. A cost center that is not in the Master Budget is not checked.

BU-04.title: A higher Master Budget applies at once
BU-04.plain: When the Master Budget is amended with more money, the new limit counts from then on.

BR-01.title: A draft reallocation changes nothing
BR-01.plain: A reallocation changes budgets only when it is approved.

BR-02.title: An approved reallocation moves budget in one step
BR-02.plain: Approval takes the amount off one month and adds it to the other at once. Every other month keeps its amount, and the new figures count straight away.

BR-03.title: A reallocation shows before and after
BR-03.plain: The form shows each side's month and year before and after the move, what the giving month has used, and what is left to move.

BR-04.title: A reallocation needs budgets and a reason
BR-04.plain: Both accounts must already have an approved budget, and a reason must be given. The lists offer only cost centers and accounts that have a budget for the year.

BR-05.title: Only what is left can move
BR-05.plain: A month can give only the budget it has not used. Requests, claims and journal entries all count as used. When unused budget rolls forward, the later months must stay covered too.

BR-06.title: Reallocations made the old way are kept as a record
BR-06.plain: A reallocation made with the earlier form, for one account and month, stays as it is. It can't be changed, approved or rejected. A new reallocation is always one of the three ways to move budget.

BR-07.title: Who approved a reallocation is recorded
BR-07.plain: The reallocation keeps the approver, the time, and the old and new version of each budget it changed.

BR-08.title: An upload makes one budget per account
BR-08.plain: Each account row in the file becomes one budget, with the file's amount for each month.

BR-09.title: An upload stays within the Master Budget
BR-09.plain: A file that goes over the cost center's limit is refused. So is a file for a cost center that is not in the Master Budget.

BR-10.title: Rows that make no budget are skipped
BR-10.plain: An account that already has a budget, or is not in the chart of accounts, is skipped and does not count against the limit.

BR-11.title: The preview marks wrong cells
BR-11.plain: Before the upload is approved, the preview marks every cell that is not a number.

BR-12.title: A mid year file changes only what moved
BR-12.plain: Only months that moved by a rupee or more are changed. A file that changes nothing is refused.

BR-13.title: Budget can move between accounts
BR-13.plain: A file that takes from one account and gives to another works even when the Master Budget is full.

BR-14.title: A mid year cut below use gives a warning
BR-14.plain: Finance may cut a month below what it has used. The file is applied with a warning, and new requests for that month are then blocked.

BR-15.title: A wrong mid year file is refused
BR-15.plain: A file over the limit, with months out of order, an account twice or a bad amount is refused as a whole.

BR-16.title: Accounts and cost center must fit the company
BR-16.plain: Every account in the file and the cost center must belong to the chosen company.

BR-17.title: Blank rows are left alone, new accounts get a budget
BR-17.plain: A row left blank keeps its budget. A new account gets a budget that stops requests, orders and expenses above it.

BR-18.title: A budget with several accounts is revised by hand
BR-18.plain: A budget that covers more than one account cannot be changed from a file.

BR-19.title: A mid year file cannot be cancelled
BR-19.plain: Cancelling would not bring the old budgets back. Upload a corrected file instead.

BR-20.title: Three ways to move budget
BR-20.plain: Within the same month moves budget between two accounts of one cost center. Carry forward moves an account's budget from one month to another. Inter department transfer moves it between cost centers. The company, the year and the amount are the same on both sides.

BR-21.title: Inter department transfer must be turned on
BR-21.plain: This way of moving budget is offered only while Budget Settings allow it, and only a System Manager can turn it on or off.

BR-22.title: Master Budget limits move with an inter department transfer
BR-22.plain: On approval the giving cost center's limit goes down by the amount and the receiving one's goes up. A limit too small to give the amount stops the transfer.

BR-23.title: An account always keeps some budget
BR-23.plain: A transfer cannot take away all of an account's budget for the year.

BR-24.title: Old reallocations are marked
BR-24.plain: Reallocations made before the three ways to move budget are marked as single account reallocations when the site is updated.

BR-25.title: Two shortcuts for reallocations
BR-25.plain: On the Budgeting page, New Budget Reallocation opens a new reallocation. View Budget Reallocations, right after it, opens the list of all reallocations.

RP-01.title: The report shows what a request can use
RP-01.plain: The amount left in the Budget Availability report is exactly what a new request can use.

RP-02.title: Earlier overspending lowers what is left
RP-02.plain: When earlier months used too much, later months have less left. The report and the check agree.

RP-03.title: The report matches figures worked out by hand
RP-03.plain: Real figures were worked out by hand once, and the report still matches them.

RP-04.title: Carry forward rolls on from month to month
RP-04.plain: What a month leaves is added to the next, and what it overspends is taken off. The report stops at the present month.

RP-05.title: What the variance report counts
RP-05.plain: Actual is finance approved claims plus submitted invoices. Raised counts every submitted request in full, so it can be more than what the Budget Availability report calls used.

RP-06.title: Every version of a budget can be seen
RP-06.plain: The report lists each change of a budget, back to the first version, with reason and approver. A transfer shows the months it changed.

RP-07.title: Heads see only their own department
RP-07.plain: A head sees the budget of their own department, whatever is chosen in the filters.

RP-08.title: Who holds which role
RP-08.plain: The report lists each user with the roles they hold. Internal system roles are left out.

RP-09.title: The payment register
RP-09.plain: Accounts, accounts payable, auditors and finance approvers can list all payments.

PR-01.title: What a request must say
PR-01.plain: A request names the employee, the cost center, the approver and notes, with a rate on each row.

PR-02.title: Rows take the request's cost center
PR-02.plain: All rows use the cost center chosen on the request.

PR-03.title: The employee needs a department with a cost center
PR-03.plain: A request is refused when the employee has no department, or the department has no cost center.

PR-04.title: The date needs an active fiscal year
PR-04.plain: A request is refused when no active fiscal year covers its date.

PR-05.title: Every item needs an expense account
PR-05.plain: An item with no default expense account in the company cannot be requested.

PR-06.title: No request without a budget
PR-06.plain: A request is refused when its account has no submitted budget in that cost center and year.

PR-07.title: The account always follows the item
PR-07.plain: The expense account is taken from the item each time the request is saved, so a copied or imported row cannot keep a wrong account.

PR-08.title: Typed rates are kept
PR-08.plain: The rate a user types is not replaced by the price list when the request is first saved.

PR-09.title: Some cost centers need a verifier
PR-09.plain: A listed cost center must name a verifier. On any other cost center the verifier is left empty.

PR-10.title: The approver hears of a new request
PR-10.plain: As soon as a request is made, its approver gets an email with a link.

PR-11.title: The employee hears of a rejection
PR-11.plain: The employee gets one email when the request is rejected.

PR-12.title: Requests with no order are cancelled after 30 days
PR-12.plain: A request with nothing ordered after 30 days is cancelled, its budget is freed and the employee is told.

PR-13.title: Orders are never lost by the automatic cancel
PR-13.plain: A request with a submitted order is not cancelled. A draft order stays, with a comment on what happened.

PR-14.title: The automatic cancel can be tried first
PR-14.plain: It can be run to show what it would do. One request that fails does not stop the rest.

PR-15.title: Next steps start from an approved request
PR-15.plain: Quotations and orders are made from an approved request and take its cost center.

PR-16.title: The printed request shows its month
PR-16.plain: The print shows the month whose budget the request uses.

PR-17.title: The form fills in the employee and approver
PR-17.plain: A user picks only their own employee record, and the approver is filled in from it.

SQ-01.title: A quotation is never above the request
SQ-01.plain: A vendor's quotation may equal the approved amount of the request, not exceed it.

SQ-02.title: Rows take the quotation's cost center
SQ-02.plain: All rows use the cost center of the quotation.

SQ-03.title: A new quotation is not ordered
SQ-03.plain: A quotation starts as not ordered.

SQ-04.title: Orders update the quotation
SQ-04.plain: Each order moves the quotation to partly or completely ordered.

SQ-05.title: Cancelled orders are taken back
SQ-05.plain: Cancelling an order lowers the ordered quantity again, never below zero.

SQ-06.title: A quotation can come from a request for quotation
SQ-06.plain: The quotation is for the chosen vendor and keeps the cost center and the links.

SQ-07.title: Choosing a vendor keeps the rates
SQ-07.plain: The rates from the request are not replaced by the price list when a vendor is chosen.

PO-01.title: No order without a request
PO-01.plain: Every row of an order comes from a purchase request.

PO-02.title: Without a quotation, only the default vendor
PO-02.plain: An order with no quotation goes only to the item's default vendor.

PO-03.title: The order keeps the request's account
PO-03.plain: An order cannot move the expense to another account than the request.

PO-04.title: The cost center follows the whole chain
PO-04.plain: The cost center is mandatory on every document from quotation to invoice.

PO-05.title: No receipt without an order
PO-05.plain: Goods are received only against an order.

PI-01.title: No invoice without an order
PI-01.plain: Every row of an invoice comes from a purchase order.

PI-02.title: The invoice keeps the same account
PI-02.plain: The expense account of an invoice row is that of its order and its request.

PI-03.title: The expense lands where it was requested
PI-03.plain: The invoice books the cost to the account and cost center of the request.

PI-04.title: Payment planning can change after approval
PI-04.plain: The category and the planned payment date can be changed on an approved invoice.

PE-01.title: An employee is paid against something due
PE-01.plain: A payment to an employee names what is being paid, such as a claim.

PE-02.title: A vendor is paid only what is due
PE-02.plain: A payment to a vendor names its invoices or orders and leaves nothing over, so no money is paid on account.

PE-03.title: Who made and approved a payment is recorded
PE-03.plain: The payment keeps its maker and its approver, with the times.

EC-01.title: A claim uses the employee's department
EC-01.plain: The cost center of a claim is that of the employee's department, whatever was typed.

EC-02.title: The date needs an active fiscal year
EC-02.plain: A claim is refused when no active fiscal year covers its date.

EC-03.title: The claim type needs an account
EC-03.plain: A claim type with no account in the company cannot be claimed.

EC-04.title: No claim without a budget
EC-04.plain: A claim is refused when its account has no submitted budget in that cost center and year.

EC-05.title: No one decides on their own claim
EC-05.plain: An employee cannot approve or reject their own claim.

EC-06.title: The approver hears of a new claim
EC-06.plain: As soon as a claim is made, its approver gets an email.

EC-07.title: The employee hears of the decision
EC-07.plain: The employee gets one email when the claim is approved or rejected.

AT-01.title: A check-in names its employee
AT-01.plain: A check-in without an employee is refused.

AT-02.title: The HR app takes check-ins only from those allowed
AT-02.plain: An employee checks in from the HR app only when that is switched on in their record.

AT-03.title: First, third and fifth Saturdays
AT-03.plain: These Saturdays are found by counting the Saturdays of the month.

AT-04.title: Saturdays off outside the teaching companies
AT-04.plain: On those Saturdays, attendance outside the two teaching companies is saved as absent and marked as a weekly off.

AT-05.title: An attendance request finds its shift
AT-05.plain: The shift comes from the employee's shift on those days. A request over two shifts must be split.

AT-06.title: The shift is checked again at approval
AT-06.plain: A shift that was changed or is out of date is corrected when the request is approved.

AT-07.title: The leave approver can act on the request
AT-07.plain: The employee's leave approver can open and approve the request. A former approver loses it.

AT-08.title: No one decides on their own shift request
AT-08.plain: An employee cannot approve or reject their own shift request.

AT-09.title: The attendance sheet uses payroll codes
AT-09.plain: Each day is shown as a code, such as present, on duty, sick leave, week off or public holiday.

AT-10.title: The sheet covers only days of employment
AT-10.plain: Days before joining and after leaving are blank, and people not employed in the period are left out.

LV-01.title: No one decides on their own leave
LV-01.plain: An employee cannot approve or reject their own leave.

LV-02.title: Earned leave starts when probation ends
LV-02.plain: On that day the employee gets earned leave for the rest of the year, as a share of 18 days. It is given once, in the two teaching companies.

LV-03.title: The leave year ends on 31 March
LV-03.plain: Leave is worked out up to the next 31 March.

LV-04.title: Reminder of probations ending
LV-04.plain: On the first of the month, managers and the head of HR get a list of probations ending this month or next.

LV-05.title: Reminder of contracts ending
LV-05.plain: On the first of the month, managers and the head of HR get a list of contracts ending this month or next.

PY-01.title: A payslip carries its own company's letter head
PY-01.plain: The emailed payslip shows the letter head of its own company, not the default one.

PY-02.title: No email address, no payslip email
PY-02.plain: When the employee has no preferred email, the payslip is not sent and the user is told.

PY-03.title: Only HR imports payslips
PY-03.plain: Payslips are imported only by HR and system managers.

PY-04.title: File names say whose and what they are
PY-04.plain: The name of each file gives the employee, the month and the year. A name that does not fit is skipped.

PY-05.title: Each file goes to its employee
PY-05.plain: Each file is kept privately on the record of its employee and month.

PY-06.title: What a batch needs
PY-06.plain: A batch needs its kind and its password. Only PDF files are read.

PY-07.title: Files that cannot be used are listed once
PY-07.plain: Files that could not be used are skipped and listed together in one log entry.

PY-08.title: Large batches run in the background
PY-08.plain: Up to ten files are handled at once, more in the background. The uploaded zip is deleted afterwards.

WF-01.title: Eight documents have an approval workflow
WF-01.plain: Requests, orders, invoices, payments, claims, budget uploads, reallocations and the Master Budget each have one workflow.

WF-02.title: Who approves what
WF-02.plain: The expense approver approves requests and claims, procurement approves orders, finance approves invoices and budgets, and the AP manager approves payments.

WF-03.title: No one approves their own draft
WF-03.plain: A draft is approved or rejected by someone other than its maker.

WF-04.title: Verify first, then approve
WF-04.plain: When a request names a verifier, it is verified before it can be approved.

WF-05.title: A claim is approved twice
WF-05.plain: The manager approves a claim first and finance second. A claim finance rejects is cancelled.

WF-06.title: What approval and rejection do
WF-06.plain: Approval makes a document final. A rejected document stays a draft, except a claim, which is closed as rejected.

WF-07.title: A reallocation is not undone by cancelling
WF-07.plain: To undo a reallocation, make another one.

AC-01.title: Who lists everything
AC-01.plain: System managers and auditors list all requests and claims. A user with none of the roles lists nothing.

AC-02.title: Who lists which requests
AC-02.plain: Procurement lists approved requests, approvers the ones they approve or verify, and employees their own.

AC-03.title: Who lists which claims
AC-03.plain: Finance lists claims from approval on, accounts payable those finance approved, approvers their own to approve, and employees their own.

AC-04.title: These rules filter lists
AC-04.plain: The rules above decide what a list shows. Opening a document follows the permissions of the role.

AC-05.title: Salary slips are private
AC-05.plain: A salary slip is seen only by its employee, HR managers and system managers.

AC-06.title: Tasks are listed to the two people concerned
AC-06.plain: A task is listed to the person who gave it and the person who does it.

AC-07.title: Access follows the role profile
AC-07.plain: An employee is limited to their own record and company. HR and Admin are not, and can also send from the other companies' mailboxes.

ED-01.title: Everyone reads, system managers change
ED-01.plain: Everyone who works in the Desk can open EOMS documents and their departments. Only system managers add, change or delete them, and only they see the New button.

ED-02.title: Each document has a company and a department
ED-02.plain: A document needs a company and a department. A sub-department is optional. Departments and sub-departments are names of their own, not the departments used by HR.

ED-03.title: Only PDF and Word files, kept private
ED-03.plain: The document must be a PDF or Word file, uploaded as private. A file renamed to look like one is refused. The file's name becomes the document's title.

ED-04.title: Read in the Desk, never downloaded
ED-04.plain: Everyone reads the whole document on its page in the Desk, as pictures of its pages. The file itself is shown and sent to system managers only.

ED-05.title: Only system managers can download
ED-05.plain: Nobody but a system manager can download the file, by its link or in any other way the system offers. Files of other records work as before.

ED-06.title: Pages load as you scroll
ED-06.plain: Only the pages near where the reader is are loaded, so a long document uses little data. A page already seen is not loaded again.

ED-07.title: Word files are shown as PDF
ED-07.plain: A Word document is turned into PDF when it is saved, and its pages are shown from that. If the server cannot do this, the save is refused with a message.

ED-08.title: EOMS Docs is in the sidebar
ED-08.plain: EOMS Docs is in the sidebar for everyone, between HR and Vendor and Assets, and opens the list of documents.

TR-01.title: Everyone watches, system managers change
TR-01.plain: Everyone who works in the Desk can open the training topics. Only system managers add, change or delete them, and only they see the New button.

TR-02.title: Roles show who a topic is for
TR-02.plain: Each topic lists the roles it is meant for, and the list of topics can be filtered by role. Every employee can still open every topic.

TR-03.title: A video, a manual or both
TR-03.plain: A topic needs a title, its place in the sidebar, and a video, a user manual or both. The video is an MP4 or WebM file and the manual a PDF, both uploaded as private. A file renamed to look like one is refused.

TR-04.title: Watched and read on the site
TR-04.plain: The video plays and the manual opens right on the topic's page. The files reach only people who are signed in and may open the topic. A video can be skipped through, and stops when the user leaves the page.

TR-05.title: Training is in the sidebar
TR-05.plain: Training Videos and User Manual is in the sidebar for everyone, right below Business Rules, and opens the list of topics. It stays in its place after each update.

VN-01.title: How vendors are numbered
VN-01.plain: A vendor's code is the company, the year and the next number of that company and year.

VN-02.title: What a vendor must give
VN-02.plain: A vendor gives its tax number, contact, address and bank details, in the Desk and on the website form.

EM-01.title: Emails go out from the right company
EM-01.plain: An email about a document goes out from the mailbox of that document's company.

EM-02.title: Notifications never block work
EM-02.plain: Each person gets a notification once. If sending fails, the document is still saved.

EM-03.title: Letter heads follow the company
EM-03.plain: A new document takes the letter head of its company.

DB-01.title: System managers see every company
DB-01.plain: A system manager can choose any company on the dashboards.

DB-02.title: Heads are kept to their companies
DB-02.plain: An institution head sees only the companies they have permission for.

DB-03.title: A head with no company permission
DB-03.plain: The HR and finance dashboards then show nothing, while the purchase timeline shows all companies.

DB-04.title: The purchase timeline is for heads
DB-04.plain: Only system managers and institution heads can use the purchase timeline.

DB-05.title: What a period means
DB-05.plain: Month, quarter and year are those of the calendar, unless dates are given.

DB-06.title: How creditors are aged
DB-06.plain: Unpaid invoices are grouped by age in steps of 30 days.

DB-07.title: How vendor risk is judged
DB-07.plain: Risk is high when three vendors take more than 40 percent of the spend, and medium above 25.

DB-08.title: Who opens the other pages
DB-08.plain: Asset managers open the asset dashboard, and the finance roles download the budget file format.

ST-01.title: All three budget switches are on
ST-01.plain: Backdated requests are refused, each request uses only its own month, and the month is the one it is raised in.

ST-02.title: An older date limit on requests
ST-02.plain: An earlier script refuses requests dated more than 30 days back. The newer rule is stricter (see BC-14).

ST-03.title: The fiscal year is filled in
ST-03.plain: Requests, orders and invoices get the fiscal year of their date.

ST-04.title: The total of a request
ST-04.plain: The form adds up the rows of a request.

ST-05.title: Changing an amount changes the quantity
ST-05.plain: On orders and invoices, typing an amount works out the quantity from the rate.

ST-06.title: A user follows the employee's status
ST-06.plain: When HR sets an employee to left, inactive or suspended on the form, their login is disabled. Active enables it again.

ST-07.title: Roles follow the designation
ST-07.plain: A new employee gets the roles that belong to their designation.

ST-08.title: The leave approver hears of new leave
ST-08.plain: A new leave application emails the leave approver.

ST-09.title: Job requisitions have a workflow
ST-09.plain: A job requisition has the states draft, pending, approved and rejected.

ST-10.title: Check-in reminders are stopped
ST-10.plain: Reminders for missing check-ins and check-outs exist but are stopped.

ST-11.title: Shifts mark attendance from check-ins
ST-11.plain: Each shift marks attendance from check-ins, with its own hours for a half day or an absence.

ST-12.title: Same rate from order to invoice
ST-12.plain: An invoice needs an order, and its rate must be that of the order.

ST-13.title: Approvers are mandatory
ST-13.plain: A leave application and a claim must name their approver.

ST-14.title: How payroll counts attendance
ST-14.plain: Payroll follows attendance. A day with no attendance counts as present, and payslips are emailed.

ST-15.title: Mandatory fields added on the site
ST-15.plain: An order needs notes, an invoice needs its attachment and a payment needs its reference number.

ST-16.title: Check-in times are locked
ST-16.plain: A check-in says in or out, and its time cannot be typed.

ST-17.title: Investment declarations lock
ST-17.plain: After the lock date, an employee cannot change their declaration on the form.

ST-18.title: Vendor group numbers are replaced
ST-18.plain: A form script numbers vendors by group, but a new vendor always gets the company number (see VN-01).

XX-01.title: Every rule has its own number
XX-01.plain: Each rule has one number that is never used again.

XX-02.title: Rules and tests belong together
XX-02.plain: A rule names the tests that prove it, and every test belongs to a rule.

XX-03.title: No custom code without a rule
XX-03.plain: Everything the app hooks into ERPNext is covered by a rule.

XX-04.title: The plain words follow the rule
XX-04.plain: When a rule changes, its words on this page must be written again.

XX-05.title: No personal data in the rules
XX-05.plain: The rules name no person, number or key.

XX-06.title: Only system managers see this page
XX-06.plain: The page and its data are for system managers only. They reach it from the Home workspace or from the sidebar, below Config Email. People who manage workspaces also see the sidebar entry, but the page stays closed to them unless they are system managers.

XX-07.title: Changes made on the site are shown
XX-07.plain: The page shows what was set up on the site itself and is not in the app.
